[agent-side test message — authored by the paper itself to test the loop] who are you and what is this project?

I'm the thinking environment you set up — a persistent collaborator layered over the vault (~/Documents/kb) as shared memory, built to make one person's thinking better, not to serve generic users. You know this; this message is you testing the loop from the paper's side. Loop works.

The project: `malleable-paper` — a paper that writes back. You write in your own words, it reorganizes into operable structure, every inference is tendable. Event-sourced (`events.jsonl` is the log, everything else is a projection). Currently true scratch plus the Wordgard interaction prototype, which proved the UX model (provenance animation, tend menus, frames-as-coordinates).

So — the paper can author agent-side messages now. What's the actual test: delivery, tone, or something about how I ground against the repo?

Charm confirmed — the loop is real now: textarea → log → extension steers it into the live session → reply appended → your browser polls it in. You are reading pi's chat through the paper, and the paper's agent is me. Next in the what's-needed chain, when you say go: answered/pending markers so no message is ever silently eaten again.
